content.content:
An id listed in one of the detail panel's four relationship sections that names a node document is drawn in the link colour role: the entry's text takes the colour the graph already draws links in, so a reader meets the id as something to follow. The role is committed for every such entry, in all four sections — "depends_on", "evaluates", "dependents" and "evaluators" — and for an id that names a decision and one that names an evaluation alike, because an evaluation's id leads to a node exactly as a decision's does (mwwxxzyk, zkvxornu). An id listed in two sections is the same id and takes the same role in both.

The role is the one already recorded, not a colour chosen here. oqotyplt records the link colour role as the token --vscode-textLink-foreground, and this decision spends that role on the entry as it is recorded: the entry's text is drawn in that token, the entry is given no colour of its own, and in being spent on the entry the role is given no second meaning and no altered value — it is still one role, the graph's link colour, and not a variant of it for the panel. What the token resolves to, the colour a theme actually paints, is the token's and the theme's, so the entry reads in the link colour a light theme and a dark one each provide; the decision fixes which role the entry takes, not a literal colour value. The role likewise says nothing about which section the entry sits in or which field named it: the section and the recorded edge carry that (rmovtvkt), and colour alone does not.

Colouring the entry is the whole of what this decision does to it. The entry's text stays the bare id (mwwxxzyk): the role is applied to the characters the entry already shows, so the id the reader follows is still the id the field holds, with no label, no summary, no short form and no further emphasis arriving alongside the colour. The decision fixes the entry's text colour and nothing else about how the entry is drawn: it names no element to carry the colour, no class or other vocabulary to select the entry by, and no stylesheet rule; and it states the role for the entry as it rests in its section, saying nothing about how the entry is drawn while a pointer is over it or while it has focus. The pointer cue, the hover treatment and the focus marking are each a separate commitment; none of them is required, forbidden or implied here.

This decision does not make the entry a link. That a listed id is presented as a visible link, set apart from the plain text of its section, is mwwxxzyk's; this decision takes the colour one part of that presentation is drawn in, and takes it presupposing the link rather than establishing it. Nor does it settle the appearance of a listed id that names no node document: that entry is listed among its siblings and stays inert (rusopkql), and its appearance belongs to decisions that own that case, which may draw it in this role or in a different colour as they settle. The link colour role is committed here for the listed entry that names a node, and is neither required nor forbidden for the entry that names none.
content.rationale:
mwwxxzyk committed a listed id that names a node to reading as a link and then stopped short of the entry's colour, so the entry is a link whose drawn colour is unstated: on a plain panel it would sit in the section's ordinary text colour and the link-ness would rest entirely on the other parts of the presentation a later decision gives it, leaving the most familiar cue a reader has for a followable id unspent. The link colour role is that cue, and filling it is exactly the gap mwwxxzyk left: it is an appearance fact about an entry that exists, so it adds nothing to what is listed, nothing to what activating an entry does and no element to the section.

The role is taken from oqotyplt rather than invented, because the graph already draws its links in that role: the dependency edge a section reports is drawn in --vscode-textLink-foreground, and an entry that reports one end of that edge is the same thing to follow, so the panel says "followable" in the colour the canvas already says it in. Spending the recorded role keeps one meaning for that colour across the canvas and the panel, and it keeps the role in one place: had this decision named a colour of its own, or given the link role a distinct panel variant, the token would have two values to keep in step and a reader could no longer rely on the colour meaning the same thing in both places.

Stopping at the colour is what keeps the rest decidable on its own terms. The pointer cursor, the hover treatment, the focus marking, which element carries the colour and the class vocabulary are each verifiable in the styles, so each belongs to the decision that owns it; settled here they would either be restated or contradicted by those decisions, and this one would have decided an entry's whole presentation in the course of deciding its colour. Bounding the commitment to the entry as it rests, and to the characters already shown, keeps the text and the section's contents out of it as well: the id stays the id, and the colour is the only thing the reader gains.

Leaving the id that names no node document out is the same restraint rusopkql applied when it kept that entry listed and inert. That entry cannot be followed, so whether it is drawn as the different case it is — muted, or in the link colour like its siblings — is a judgement its own decisions have to make; fixing the link colour for every listed id here would decide it by accident, and forbidding it would decide it just as surely the other way. The colour belongs to the entry that names a node; the entry that names none keeps its appearance open.
